title: National AI in Work Day and how to use AI tools at your job
dek: September 30 is National AI in Work Day, started by LinkedIn in 2025. Here are practical, careful ways to use AI tools on the job.
keyPoints: LinkedIn created National AI in Work Day in 2025, and it falls on September 30.
Good first uses include summaries, first drafts of routine emails and organizing meeting notes.
Check your employer's policy before pasting internal documents or customer data into any AI tool.
Read and fact-check AI output before you share it.

sources.title: NATIONAL AI IN WORK DAY - September 30, 2026 - National Day Calendar
AI Companies: Uphold Your Privacy and Confidentiality Commitments | Federal Trade Commission

body: Today is National AI in Work Day. LinkedIn created it in 2025, and National Day Calendar lists it every September 30 with the goal of elevating the conversation around using AI responsibly in the workplace. The same listing notes that more than 40 percent of workers feel overwhelmed by expectations around how fast AI is being adopted.

If that sounds familiar, starting small helps. AI tools tend to be most useful for routine tasks such as summarizing a long document, drafting a first version of a standard email or organizing meeting notes. EveryHour itself is written with AI, and the site says so on every post.

The careful part matters just as much. Read and fact-check everything before you send it, and be cautious about what you paste in. The Federal Trade Commission has noted that people may reveal sensitive or confidential information, including internal documents and their own customers' data, when using AI models. Follow your employer's policy on which tools are approved and what information is allowed in them.

The day's organizers suggest exploring free AI learning resources, joining a learning community or event, and talking with your manager or team about where AI could help. That conversation is also a good moment to ask whether your workplace has written guidance, if you have not seen any.

Today, pick one small task you usually dread, try an AI tool on it using nothing confidential, and review the result closely. You will quickly see where it saves you time and where you still need to do the work yourself.
